article_content: A young boy who has survived nine life-saving operations has delighted his parents by coming home for the first time. Fourteen-month-old Aaron Armstrong had spent his entire life in hospital after being diagnosed with a rare genetic disorder. He faces developmental challenges, including heart, facial, and growth defects, and has been treated at Freeman Hospital in Newcastle. Even though Aaron is not speaking yet, he smiles and grabs at objects, bringing joy to his parents, Elaine (44) and Alan (42), from Rowlands Gill, Gateshead. Alan, who serves in the Parachute Regiment, shared: 'Elaine and I are over the moon to have Aaron home. It's wonderful to spend time alone with him. We're beginning to see light at the end of the tunnel. Aaron is improving, building strength, and interacting more. He reaches for things and gently touches our faces. In the mornings, he wakes up with a smile for us.' At birth, tests revealed Aaron had a hole in his heart and other cardiac problems. He was also diagnosed with chromosome 8.21 deletion syndrome, with doctors warning his parents about possible learning difficulties and physical delays. Aaron had received treatment at Freeman Hospital since May last year until coming home for the first time. Aaron is now cared for at home with the support of community nurses. He is on a ventilator, is tube-fed, and has a tracheostomy to help with breathing. The progression of Aaron's condition remains uncertain, and he has not yet started to speak. Alan added, 'Aaron is behind with his development—some children his age are starting to walk, but Aaron lies on his play mat. However, he's very determined with a lovely smile. I am very proud of him.' When Aaron was six months old, he underwent eight-hour open-heart surgery to replace a faulty valve. He has since been fitted with a mechanical heart valve and a pacemaker. Community nurses continue to monitor him, and it is hoped his tracheostomy can be removed in the future. Elaine and Alan are dedicated to raising essential funds for the Freeman Hospital's Paediatric Intensive Care Unit to thank the staff for supporting their only child. This spring, Alan plans a 69-mile fundraising run along Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland. To support Alan's Hadrian's Challenge, visit www.justgiving.com/teams/Hadrians-Challenge.

article_content: Jason Bohn secured his second PGA Tour title at the Zurich Classic in New Orleans, aided by a streak of late birdies. The 37-year-old American, who celebrated his birthday on Saturday, had to complete his rain-delayed third round on Sunday morning before shooting a five-under-par 67 in the final round to win the tournament. Bohn finished with birdies on three of the last four holes, ending at 18-under par, two shots ahead of runner-up Jeff Overton. He narrowly missed an eagle on the final hole after an impressive approach shot. "This is life changing," Bohn told the PGA Tour website. "I'm probably the only guy on the PGA Tour who has tears when he's putting out on the 18th hole. When I hit the shot on 15 and made the great putt on 16, I knew if I stayed patient I had it." Prior to this victory, Bohn's only other PGA Tour win was at the B.C. Open in 2005. Since then, he has battled several injuries, including undergoing back surgery. After his win, Bohn said he wanted to savor every moment: "I just said I probably wouldn't say much because I'm capturing all of this. I want to take this one to the grave. I want to remember every little detail that I missed on my first one." Jeff Overton finished second at 16-under, and Troy Merritt followed in third at 16-under. Meanwhile, Ian Poulter and Padraig Harrington have confirmed their participation in the European Tour's flagship PGA Championship at Wentworth, England. Both had boycotted the event for two years due to poor greens but agreed to return following course renovations led by South African golfer Ernie Els. Poulter told the UK Press Association, "It is a great championship and I am looking forward to checking out the modifications to the West Course which Ernie has undertaken. I am sure the changes will be for the better."

Bohn sluttede med birdies på tre af de sidste fire huller og endte på 18 under par, to slag foran andenpladsen Jeff Overton. Han var tæt på en eagle på det sidste hul efter et imponerende indspil. "Det her ændrer mit liv," sagde Bohn til PGA Tourens hjemmeside. "Jeg er nok den eneste på PGA Touren, der får tårer i øjnene, når jeg putter på 18. hul. Da jeg slog slaget på 15 og lavede det gode put på 16, vidste jeg, hvis jeg var tålmodig, så havde jeg den." Før denne sejr var Bohns eneste anden PGA Tour-sejr ved B.C. Open i 2005. Siden da har han kæmpet med flere skader, herunder en rygoperation. Efter sejren sagde Bohn, at han ville nyde hvert øjeblik: "Jeg sagde bare, at jeg nok ikke ville sige så meget, fordi jeg indfanger det hele. Jeg vil tage denne sejr med mig til graven. Jeg vil huske alle de små detaljer, jeg missede ved min første sejr." Jeff Overton sluttede som nummer to med 16 under par, og Troy Merritt blev nummer tre – også med 16 under par. Samtidig har Ian Poulter og Padraig Harrington bekræftet, at de deltager i European Tours prestigefyldte PGA Championship på Wentworth i England. Begge havde boykottet turneringen i to år på grund af dårlige greens, men har nu sagt ja efter banerenoveringer ledet af den sydafrikanske golfspiller Ernie Els. Jeg er sikker på, at ændringerne vil være til det bedre."

article_content: Nathalie Garcia, who led Fremantle Spain as CEO for the past decade, is now joining ITV Studios to oversee the new ITV Studios Iberia. Based in Madrid and launching soon, this new division will handle the production of well-known shows like The Voice (La Voz), The Voice Kids, and The Chase (El Cazador). Garcia will answer directly to Lisa Perrin, the Managing Director of International Production at ITV Studios. Over her career, Garcia has been responsible for producing hit programs such as Got Talent España and The Masked Singer, as well as the game show Password and the reality series The Farm. She previously held leadership positions at Plural Entertainment and Vértice 360 Group. With Garcia leaving Fremantle, Jaime Ondarza, CEO for Southern Europe, has stepped in as interim head of the company. ITV Studios considers Spain to be an energetic market, with Perrin describing Garcia as the right choice to steer their growing presence. Garcia expressed her excitement about working with such a leading company in the TV industry.

Garcia skal rapportere direkte til Lisa Perrin, Managing Director for International Production hos ITV Studios. During the thrilling ICC Cricket World Cup semi-final against New Zealand, former Indian captain Virat Kohli surpassed Sachin Tendulkar's record by achieving his 50th ODI century. While Kohli’s milestone dominated headlines, many were intrigued by the simple wrist band he wore during the match. This understated accessory has also been spotted on elite athletes like basketball star LeBron James, Olympic swimmer Michael Phelps, and top golfers including Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods.

Unlike conventional smartwatches or fitness trackers, the band lacks a screen or flashy features, drawing curiosity due to its use among renowned athletes. Known as WHOOP, this fitness wearable is developed by the US-based tech company WHOOP, founded in 2012 by Will Ahmed, a former Harvard student-athlete. WHOOP is dedicated to studying human performance and provides a subscription-based strap equipped with five sensors that collect a broad array of physiological data.

Pairing with an app, WHOOP gives users insights into daily recovery, cardiovascular strain, training load, and sleep quality. Its sensors monitor heart rate, heart rate variability, ambient temperature, movement, and skin conductivity. The device generates approximately 100MB of data daily, all visualized through the WHOOP app—available on both mobile and desktop platforms for comprehensive trend analysis. The app is personalized, adapting over several days to establish the user’s baseline data.

By analyzing blood flow and heartbeats, WHOOP determines heart rate and variability, crucial for assessing recovery. Its sleep cycle analysis relies on continuous monitoring during specific sleep stages, enhancing accuracy and consistency. The system evaluates recovery status, indicating fatigue or readiness for intense training, and essentially acts as a digital personal coach—explaining its popularity among elite athletes.

Alongside tracking sleep patterns and assessing sleep quality, WHOOP’s app provides detailed visualizations and long-term trends. The Strain Coach, one of its standout features, offers daily training recommendations based on users’ recovery and current strain, optimizing workouts.

WHOOP is built with a durable Onyx SuperKnit band and features a waterproof, wireless battery, boasting five-day battery life and an IP68 rating (water-resistant up to 10 meters for 2 hours). The company pioneered the subscription model for fitness wearables, with current annual pricing at $239 (down from $300), a two-year plan at $399 (down from $480), and a monthly subscription (with a 12-month commitment) at $30. It offers 28 color options, with extensive customization—up to 74,000 possible combinations—and comes with a lifetime warranty and 24/7 customer support.

Additionally, WHOOP partners with health and fitness brands for exclusive giveaways, apparel, and accessories. The device is available in 40 countries, though it has not yet launched in India.

Will Ahmed began WHOOP driven by his passion for sports and fitness, stemming from his childhood and experiences as a Harvard squash athlete. Inspired by a desire to better understand his body and prevent overtraining, he undertook physiology research that ultimately led to the founding of WHOOP. Despite the company’s current success, Ahmed openly discussed past financial challenges, including times when the startup was nearly bankrupt. WHOOP debuted its first device in 2015 and has since launched several updated versions, most recently WHOOP 4.0 in 2021.

While WHOOP has earned acclaim—especially among elite athletes—there are important considerations for potential users. Compared to smartwatches like Apple Watch or Garmin, which can track similar metrics, WHOOP distinguishes itself with its focus on recovery analytics and flexible form factor (it can be worn on the wrist, biceps, or embedded in apparel). However, it is most valuable for users wanting in-depth recovery and sleep analysis, less so for those needing broader activity or non-cardio tracking. The subscription model and limited functionality compared to multi-purpose smartwatches mean WHOOP is best suited for serious athletes and dedicated fitness enthusiasts, though its tracking capabilities are highly regarded.

Under den spændende ICC Cricket World Cup-semifinale mod New Zealand slog den tidligere indiske kaptajn Virat Kohli Sachin Tendulkars rekord ved at opnå sin 50. ODI-century. Dette diskrete tilbehør er også set på elitesportsfolk som basketballstjernen LeBron James, olympisk svømmer Michael Phelps og golfspillere som Rory McIlroy og Tiger Woods.

I modsætning til almindelige smartwatches eller fitness trackers har armbåndet hverken skærm eller andre iøjnefaldende funktioner, hvilket gør det interessant, fordi det bæres af kendte atleter. Det hedder WHOOP og er udviklet af det amerikanske teknologifirma WHOOP, grundlagt i 2012 af Will Ahmed, tidligere Harvard-studerende og atlet. WHOOP fokuserer på studiet af menneskelig præstation og leverer et abonnementbaseret armbånd med fem sensorer, som indsamler en bred vifte af fysiologiske data.

WHOOP sammen med en app giver brugerne indsigt i daglig restitution, hjerte-kar-belastning, træningsmængde og søvnkvalitet. Sensorerne overvåger puls, hjertevariabilitet, omgivelsestemperatur, bevægelse og hudens ledningsevne. Enheden genererer omkring 100MB data dagligt, som visualiseres gennem WHOOP-appen – tilgængelig både på mobil og computer for at give brugerne detaljeret indsigt over tid. Appen tilpasses individuelt og indsamler basisdata over flere dage.

Ved at analysere blodgennemstrømning og hjerteslag kan WHOOP måle puls og variabilitet, som er vigtige for at vurdere restitution. Søvncykelanalysen bygger på kontinuerlig overvågning i specifikke søvnstadier, hvilket forbedrer nøjagtighed og konsistens. Systemet vurderer restitution og indikerer, om du er træt eller klar til hård træning, og fungerer i praksis som en digital personlig træner – hvilket forklarer dets popularitet blandt elitesportsfolk.

WHOOP tracker også søvnmønstre og -kvalitet, og appen giver detaljerede visualiseringer og langtidsanalyser. Strain Coach, en af de fremtrædende funktioner, foreslår daglige træningsniveauer ud fra restitution og belastning for at optimere dit træningsudbytte.

WHOOP er bygget med et slidstærkt Onyx SuperKnit-armbånd og har et vandtæt, trådløst batteri, der holder i fem dage, og en IP68-klassificering (vandafvisende op til 10 meter i 2 timer). Virksomheden var først med et fitnessabonnement, og prisen er nu $239 årligt (før $300), $399 for en toårig plan (før $480) og $30 pr. måned (med 12 måneders binding). Du kan vælge mellem 28 farver og op til 74.000 kombinationsmuligheder, og WHOOP leveres med livstidsgaranti og døgnbemandet kundesupport.

WHOOP samarbejder desuden med sundheds- og fitnessbranchen om eksklusive konkurrencer, tøj og tilbehør. Enheden er tilgængelig i 40 lande, men er endnu ikke lanceret i Indien.

Will Ahmed startede WHOOP drevet af sin passion for sport og fitness fra sin barndom og tiden som Harvard-squashspiller. Inspireret af at forstå kroppen bedre og undgå overtræning begyndte han forskning i fysiologi, som førte til WHOOP. Trods nutidig succes fortalte Ahmed åbent om tidligere økonomiske udfordringer – blandt andet perioder, hvor virksomheden næsten gik konkurs. WHOOP's første enhed kom på markedet i 2015, og de seneste opdateringer, senest WHOOP 4.0, blev lanceret i 2021.

Selvom WHOOP især er populær blandt elitesportsfolk, er der overvejelser for potentielle brugere. Sammenlignet med smartwatches som Apple Watch eller Garmin, der også kan måle lignende data, adskiller WHOOP sig ved sit fokus på restitution og fleksible design (kan bæres på håndled, overarm eller i tøj). Den er især værdifuld for dem, der ønsker dybdegående indsigt i restitution og søvn, men mindre for brugere, der ønsker mere all-round aktivitetstracking. Abonnementsmodellen og funktionalitetsbegrænsninger sammenlignet med allround-smartwatches gør WHOOP bedst egnet til seriøse atleter og fitnessentusiaster, selvom dens trackingevner roses meget.
